A vanishing point is a point on the image plane of a perspective drawing

A vanishing point is a point on the image plane of a perspective drawing where the two - dimensional perspective projections ( or drawings ) of mutually parallel lines in three - dimensional space appear to converge
When the set of parallel lines is perpendicular to a picture plane , the construction is known as one - point perspective

the construction is known as one - point perspective , and their vanishing point corresponds to the oculus , or `` eye point '' , from which the image should be viewed for correct perspective geometry
Traditional linear drawings use objects with one to three sets of parallels
Traditional linear drawings use objects with one to three sets of parallels , defining one to three vanishing points
